terms.gloss: a little seat: a child’s car seat
terms.comment: Classically a little seat or stool, and a sedan chair (Tac. H. 3.84) (Lewis & Short, which calls it post-Augustan); its use for a child’s car seat is modern, and ours. No reference work has a word for a child’s car seat. In full, sellula puerīlis; a plain description is sēdēs puerīlis, a child’s seat. The straps are the seat belt, cinctūra sēcūritātis (Traupman 218).

phrases.latin: Theodōrus post eōs in sēde puerīlī
phrases.english: Theo behind them in the child seat

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 218.
